5. Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Medical Research at the Faculty of Medicine The “Ph.D. in Program “Medical Research” is a 3-year (180 ECTS) structured program at the LMU’s Medical Faculty. It is open to students with a degree (Master’s, medical degree) from an institute of higher education in medicine, veterinary science, natural sciences, pharmacy, public health or a related field and offers participating students interdisciplinary courses, as well as research topic specific modules. Students are required to complete 30 ECTS in courses (methodology, practicals, seminars, skills, etc.), as well as working on their thesis (140 ECTS) and completing an oral defence (10 ECTS) at the end of the program. There are currently three core areas, as well as several associated research training groups. For more information on the Ph.D., please see https://www.med.lmu.de/de/promotion/

6. Graduate School of Systemic Neurosciences at the Faculty of Medicine The Master International Occupational Safety and Health is a two-year part-time program (60 ECTS). Students graduate with a “Master of Science (MSc)“ degree from the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. Working languages are Spanish (1st and 2nd year) and English (2nd year). The Master offers an international and interdisciplinary education in global Occupational Safety and Health with a focus on project-based learning. In order to ensure maximum flexibility and efficiency, the Master’s program is based on a blended learning concept combining on-site courses, online-modules and tutor guided work on projects. For more information please please refer towww.osh-munich.de or contact the Administration Office 0049-89-5160-2485.

Master Digital Cultural Heritage In order to complete your study program, you have to complete all Mandatory Modules . Also, you have to complete one out of the three Introductory Modules , and to choose five modules from the remaining elective modules . While choosing from the elective modules, you have to respect the following election rules: You may choose up to three Computer Science modules . These modules usually require Bachelor-level skills and knowledge in Computer Science. Please inform yourself about potential requirements before enrolling in these modules. From the modules offered in the Topics in the Study of Cultures section of the curriculum, you may likewise choose up to three modules , but you have to respect the following rules: You may choose one module from modules WP 13 to WP 29 . You may choose one module from modules WP 38-WP 43 and modules WP 45-WP 55 . You may choose one module from modules WP 44 and WP 61-WP 76 . These modules usually require previous knowledge in the respective discipline. Also, as the respective study programs are taught in German, most courses require at least a good understanding of German. Few disciplines also offer courses in English. Please contact your program coordinator in advance, if you are interested in taking courses in one of these disciplines and understand how to enroll. ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** For any questions about the curriculum and the organization of your studies, contact your program coordinator: Dr. Evan Eames ( evan.eames@lmu.de ). ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** *****

B.A. Nebenfach 'Sprache, Literatur, Kultur' Studienverlauf: Das Bachelor-Nebenfach Sprache, Literatur, Kultur (SLK) realisiert sich in zwei Pflichtmodulen (P1 und P2) und zwei Wahlpflichtmodulen (wählbar zwischen WP1: "Sprachen", WP2: "Literaturwissenschaft", WP3: "Linguistik", WP4: "Kultur- und Medienwissenschaften", WP5: "Ältere Sprachen und Kulturen"). Sie erwerben insgesamt 60 ECTS-Punkte. Im 1. Fachsemester sollten Sie das Pflichtmodul P1 (= 6 ECTS) und zusätzlich weitere Lehrveranstaltungen im Umfang von 6 ECTS-Punkten aus einem Wahlpflichtmodul Ihrer Wahl absolvieren (WP1 oder WP2 oder WP3 oder WP4 oder WP5).
